# Brew ratio: overview

For sponsors and the team: one document, readable without the factory.

## Executive summary

**The problem.** Brewing good coffee means working out water from coffee (or the reverse) at a chosen ratio. Doing it on a phone calculator every morning is slow and mistakes waste beans.

**The impact.** Consistent brews without arithmetic; success is two weeks of brews without reaching for a calculator.

| Reach | Impact | Confidence | Effort | Priority score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 per month | 1 (medium) | 80% | 0.5 person-weeks | 48 |

Reach is brews per month; Impact runs from 0.25 (minimal) to 3 (massive); Effort is rough person-weeks.

**Who benefits.** One home brewer.

**Effort and cost.** Half a person-week; no running cost, no accounts or services.

**Key risks.** Saved recipes live in one browser and can be lost; export and import reduce that.

**The decision asked.** Approve the recommended shape (a single page in the browser) so the detailed specification can start.

## What it is
A single web page: type the grams of coffee and pick a ratio, and it shows the water; or the other way round. Favourite recipes can be saved.

## How it changes people's work
Today the brewer multiplies on a calculator and keeps ratios on a sticky note. With the page, the sum is done for them and favourites are kept.

## In scope and out of scope
**In the first release:** both sums, saved favourites, export and import.

**Not in the first release:** timers, sharing, accounts.

## What happens next
The detailed specification, then building and checking it, then release on approval.
